numeric_contract.representation: sign + arbitrary-length decimal digits + base-ten exponent
numeric_contract.scaling: unit conversion shifts the exponent by an integer power of ten; no binary floating-point conversion or rounding
numeric_contract.reader_adapter: excel_reader::CellValue; JSON serialization remains tagged as {type,value}; XLSX-like values follow source openpyxl-compatible normalization, while XLS integers/bools follow source xlrd-compatible normalization

comparison: Exact Python Decimal sign/digits/exponent tuple equality; ValueError category and message equality; amount data-type membership equality; typed cell normalization, skip behavior, Decimal tuple and unit conversion compared to source importer._normalize_fast_value/_decimal_number.

checks.source_test_command: python -B -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/test_s2_units.py -k 'amount_conversion_is_exact_without_decimal_context_rounding or unit_conversion_rejects_unsupported_unit or source_amounts_convert_to_output_unit_before_engines_and_keep_other_types'

scope: Pure S2 amount-type/unit-conversion helpers plus a typed cell-value adapter that matches the source importer's XLS/XLSX normalization. It is not connected to the S2 importer, period/rule/external comparison engines, real workbook reading workflow, or report writing.
unverified: The adapter is not yet called by an S2 importer or verified against a real workbook read through excel-reader.
XLS/XLSX numeric semantics are fixture-matched to the source normalization helpers; other formats and value-origin combinations are not covered.
Binary64-to-decimal string parity is checked on the listed fixtures, not exhaustively over all finite f64 values.
Extreme exponent overflow behavior is not included in the fixture baseline.
No real business workbook, full S2 flow, target Linux package, or glibc 2.28 runtime was tested.
